ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the upper part of the figure there is a compact reagent/transition-state-related fragment, labeled “Bu₂B–OTf”, with multiple curved arrows around it; the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning: According to the label, take only the “Bu₂B–OTf” fragment. Expand the two Bu as two n-butyl chains CCCC, both connected to B, forming CCCCB(CCCC). B is then connected to O, followed by the OTf part; according to the specified expansion it is OS(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)Cl. Therefore the combination gives the SMILES: CCCCB(CCCC)OS(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)Cl.

method.method_draft: First inspect the image and isolate the compact transition-state/reagent fragment labeled “Bu2B–OTf” at the top, explicitly disregarding all curved arrows as instructed. Expand each abbreviation: write each Bu substituent as CCCC, attach both butyl chains to B, connect B to O, then expand the sulfonyl triflate-type part as OS(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)Cl. Concatenate these connectivities into a valid SMILES: CCCCB(CCCC)OS(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)Cl.

Because the task targets one depicted transition-state/reagent fragment and asks to ignore arrows, there is little room for genuinely independent solution strategies.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the upper structure label as Bu2B–OTf, with boron bonded to two butyl groups and through oxygen to a sulfonyl perfluoro/halodifluoromethyl triflate-type group; ignore the curved arrows and the lower amide/amine reaction components since they are mechanistic annotations rather than the requested standalone structure.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text only to determine that the required output is a SMILES string and that arrows in the image should be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use chemical shorthand rules: Bu means a normal butyl chain, Bu2B means boron attached to two n-butyl substituents, and OTf is expanded as an O–S(=O)(=O)–C(F)(F)Cl group under the answer convention. Apply standard SMILES valence/connectivity notation to combine the fragments as CCCC–B(CCCC)–O–S(=O)(=O)–C(F)(F)Cl.
